question: Which of the following decomposition reactions is NOT a redox reaction?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Decomposition of calcium carbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The decomposition of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) results in the formation of calcium oxide (CaO) and carbon dioxide (CO₂).
 
• This reaction is represented by the equation: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂.
 
• The oxidation states of the elements do not change during this decomposition reaction, indicating it is not a redox reaction.
 
• In contrast, decomposition reactions that are redox reactions involve changes in the oxidation states of the participating elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decomposition Reactions**

 
 
• A decomposition reaction is a type of chemical reaction in which a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler compounds or elements.
 
• These reactions often require an input of energy in the form of heat, light, or electricity.
 
• Examples include the decomposition of water into hydrogen and oxygen (2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂) and the decomposition of potassium chlorate into potassium chloride and oxygen (2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂).
 
 
 
• **Redox Reactions**
 
 
• Redox reactions, or oxidation-reduction reactions, involve the transfer of electrons between two substances.
 
• Oxidation refers to the loss of electrons, while reduction refers to the gain of electrons.
 
• In a redox reaction, one substance is oxidized (loses electrons) and another is reduced (gains electrons).
 
• An example is the decomposition of sodium hydride (NaH), where NaH decomposes into sodium metal (Na) and hydrogen gas (H₂), with sodium being reduced and hydrogen being oxidized.
 
 
 
• **Oxidation States**
 
 
• The oxidation state (or number) of an element in a compound is a measure of the degree of oxidation of that element.
 
• It is defined as the charge an atom would have if all bonds were completely ionic.
 
• Changes in oxidation states during a reaction indicate a redox process.
